title: Renyi-half effective count controls growing translated Gaussian mixtures at the profiled coefficient

renyi_rigidity.mixing_gain: K1606 and K1611 give 0<=sum_i p_i Q_N(nu_i)-Q_N(nu_N)<=C_g Lambda_N[R_(1/2)(p_N)-1], with Lambda_N=O_g(N).
renyi_rigidity.component_floor: K1572/K1602 bound every translated stationary diagonal Gaussian component in the fixed relative band below by lambda_N^prof.
renyi_rigidity.coefficient: If R_(1/2)(p_N)=o(N^3), then lambda_N^prof-o(N^4)<=Q_N(nu_N); since the class contains the profiled Gaussian, its infimum divided by N^4 converges to h_g^prof.
renyi_rigidity.examples: Every fixed mixture has O_g(N) gain. For equal weights R_(1/2)=M_N, so M_N=o(N^3) is sufficient. Nonuniform weights may support more nominal atoms when their effective count is subcubic.
renyi_rigidity.scope_guard: Critical or supercritical effective count, non-Gaussian components, arbitrary covariance eigenvectors, phases, textures, and nonstationarity remain open.
